name: Structure of Dismantlable-Complement Ample Classes
statement: The dismantlable-complement class $\mathsf{coDamp}$ is closed under nonempty sections, projections, full reductions, and constant-coordinate changes. It is incomparable with dismantlable ample classes, while $\mathcal B\subsetneq\mathsf{coDamp}\subsetneq\mathcal A$, and $\mathsf{MaxMin}$ is not contained in their union. The open inclusions $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}\subseteq\mathsf{Ext}$ and $\mathsf{coDamp}\subseteq\mathsf{Rep}$ are equivalent; likewise $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}\subseteq\mathsf{MaxMin}$ and $\mathsf{coDamp}\subseteq\mathsf{MaxMin}$ are equivalent.
proof: Complementation commutes with sections and exchanges projection with full reduction, so dismantlable closure laws transfer. Hall's class and its dismantlable complement witness both directions of incomparability. Their product is maximum-generated, while it and its complement each have a nondismantlable Hall section, proving the stronger noncontainment. The universal-extension complementary-shore criterion gives the first equivalence; complement closure of maximum ancestry gives the second.
